# IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF ILLINOIS, EASTERN DIVISION

**GREYSTONE PACKAGING CO.**, an Ohio corporation, Plaintiff,

v.

**TALBOT FRESH FOODS, INC.**, a Delaware corporation, Defendant.

Case No. 1:26-cv-09184

**COMPLAINT** — JURY TRIAL DEMANDED

Plaintiff Greystone Packaging Co. ("Greystone"), by its attorneys, for its Complaint against Defendant Talbot Fresh Foods, Inc. ("Talbot"), alleges as follows:

## NATURE OF THE ACTION

1. This is an action for breach of a written supply contract under which Talbot agreed to purchase minimum annual quantities of flexible food packaging from Greystone and then, after failing to meet its commitments, purported to terminate the contract to escape them.

## PARTIES, JURISDICTION AND VENUE

2. Greystone is an Ohio corporation with its principal place of business in Akron, Ohio.

3. Talbot is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in Joliet, Illinois.

4. This Court has subject-matter jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a) because the parties are citizens of different States and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs.

5. Venue is proper in this District under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1) because Talbot resides in this District.

## FACTS

6. On March 1, 2023, Greystone and Talbot entered into a Packaging Supply Agreement (the "Agreement"), a true and correct copy of which is attached as Exhibit A.

7. Under Section 4 of the Agreement, Talbot agreed to purchase Products with an aggregate invoice value of not less than $2,500,000 in each Contract Year.

8. In Contract Year 2 (March 1, 2024 through February 28, 2025), Talbot purchased Products totalling $1,887,600, leaving a shortfall of $612,400.

9. Greystone invoiced Talbot for the Contract Year 2 shortfall on March 31, 2025. Talbot has refused to pay.

10. On August 15, 2025, Talbot sent Greystone a letter purporting to terminate the Agreement for cause. Talbot's purported termination was pretextual: any quality concerns had been addressed, and Talbot simply wished to move its business to a lower-cost supplier.

11. In Contract Year 3 (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026), Talbot purchased Products totalling $1,269,800, leaving a shortfall of $1,230,200.

12. Greystone has performed all conditions precedent to the commencement of this action, or such conditions have been waived or excused.

## COUNT I — BREACH OF CONTRACT

13. Greystone incorporates paragraphs 1 through 12.

14. The Agreement is a valid and enforceable contract. Greystone performed its obligations under it.

15. Talbot breached the Agreement by failing to purchase the minimum annual quantities and by failing to pay the shortfall amounts for Contract Years 2 and 3, totalling $1,842,600.

## COUNT II — CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES

16. Greystone incorporates paragraphs 1 through 15.

17. As a direct result of Talbot's wrongful termination, Greystone idled its Line 4 laminating capacity and lost profits on the business it had reserved for Talbot in the amount of $415,000.

## PRAYER FOR RELIEF

WHEREFORE Greystone requests judgment against Talbot (a) for $1,842,600 on Count I; (b) for $415,000 on Count II; (c) for pre- and post-judgment interest and costs; and (d) for such further relief as the Court deems just.

# PACKAGING SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Packaging Supply Agreement (the "Agreement") is made as of March 1, 2023 (the "Effective Date") between **Greystone Packaging Co.**, an Ohio corporation ("Supplier"), and **Talbot Fresh Foods, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("Buyer").

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Contract Year" means each twelve-month period beginning on March 1, the first Contract Year beginning on the Effective Date.

1.2 "Products" means the laminated flexible pouches and lidding films described in Schedule 1, manufactured to the Specifications.

## 3. TERM

3.1 This Agreement continues for three (3) Contract Years from the Effective Date unless terminated earlier under Section 9.

## 4. MINIMUM PURCHASE COMMITMENT

4.1 Buyer shall purchase Products having an aggregate invoice value of not less than $2,500,000 in each Contract Year (the "Minimum Annual Purchase").

4.2 Supplier shall invoice any shortfall within thirty (30) days after the end of the Contract Year, and Buyer shall pay the invoice within thirty (30) days.

4.3 If Buyer's purchases in a Contract Year are less than the Minimum Annual Purchase, Buyer's sole liability for the shortfall shall be a fee equal to thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between the Minimum Annual Purchase and Buyer's actual purchases in that Contract Year (the "Shortfall Fee"). The parties agree that the Shortfall Fee represents Supplier's lost margin and is a reasonable pre-estimate of Supplier's damages.

## 7. QUALITY AND WARRANTY

7.1 Supplier warrants that all Products will conform to the Specifications and be free from defects in materials and workmanship, including seal and laminate integrity.

7.2 Buyer may reject any lot in which more than two percent (2%) of sampled units fail the Specifications.

## 9. TERMINATION

9.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach.

9.4 Upon termination by Buyer under Section 9.2, Buyer shall have no further minimum purchase obligations under Section 4 for the Contract Year in which termination occurs or any later Contract Year.

## 12. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

12.1 IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS OR LOSS OF BUSINESS, ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. THIS SECTION 12.1 DOES NOT LIMIT THE SHORTFALL FEE UNDER SECTION 4.3.

## 14. DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 A party asserting a dispute arising out of this Agreement shall give the other party written notice of the dispute (a "Notice of Dispute").

14.2 For thirty (30) days after delivery of a Notice of Dispute, senior executives of the parties with authority to settle shall meet and negotiate in good faith to resolve the dispute.

14.3 If the dispute is not resolved within that thirty-day period, either party may submit the dispute to non-binding mediation administered by JAMS in Chicago, Illinois. No party may commence litigation concerning a dispute until the mediation has concluded or sixty (60) days have passed after the request for mediation, except to seek temporary injunctive relief.

## 15. GENERAL

15.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Illinois.

15.2 **Notices.** Notices to Buyer shall be sent to: Talbot Fresh Foods, Inc., Attention: General Counsel, 1800 Rowell Avenue, Joliet, Illinois 60433.

15.3 **Contractual Limitations Period.** No action arising out of this Agreement may be brought by either party more than one (1) year after the cause of action has accrued.

GREYSTONE PACKAGING CO. — By: /s/ Harold Imbriano, President

TALBOT FRESH FOODS, INC. — By: /s/ Celeste Marchetti, Chief Operating Officer

# KEY CORRESPONDENCE — GREYSTONE / TALBOT

*Compiled by Talbot Fresh Foods Legal from the company's files, in date order.*

---

### Item 1 — Greystone invoice, March 31, 2025

**From:** Greystone Packaging Co., Accounts Receivable
**To:** Talbot Fresh Foods, Accounts Payable
**Date:** March 31, 2025
**Re:** Invoice GP-2025-0331 — Contract Year 2 shortfall

Contract Year 2 Minimum Annual Purchase: $2,500,000. Actual purchases: $1,887,600. Shortfall amount due: $612,400. Payment terms: net 30.

---

### Item 2 — Talbot letter disputing invoice, April 15, 2025

**From:** Celeste Marchetti, Chief Operating Officer, Talbot Fresh Foods
**To:** Harold Imbriano, President, Greystone Packaging Co.
**Date:** April 15, 2025

Harold — we dispute Invoice GP-2025-0331. Section 4.3 of our Agreement limits any Shortfall Fee to 35% of the shortfall, not the full shortfall amount. We will not pay an invoice that disregards the contract. — Celeste

---

### Item 3 — Talbot notice of breach, June 3, 2025

**From:** Priya Venkataraman, Director of Quality Assurance, Talbot Fresh Foods
**To:** Harold Imbriano, President, Greystone Packaging Co.
**Date:** June 3, 2025
**Re:** Notice of material breach under Section 9.2 — laminate delamination

This is written notice under Section 9.2 of the Packaging Supply Agreement. Lots GP-25-1187 through GP-25-1203 delivered in May 2025 show laminate delamination at the seal in 11% of sampled pouches, against a 2% rejection threshold under Section 7.2. Delaminated pouches lose their barrier and cause spoilage. Please cure within thirty (30) days of this notice.

---

### Item 4 — Greystone reply, June 20, 2025

**From:** Harold Imbriano, President, Greystone Packaging Co.
**To:** Priya Venkataraman; cc Celeste Marchetti
**Date:** June 20, 2025

Priya — our engineers have traced the delamination to an adhesive application fault on Line 4 that began after a coater rebuild in April. We have adjusted the coat weight and expect conforming product from Line 4 by July 15. We apologize for the disruption. — Harold

---

### Item 5 — Talbot QA report, July 22, 2025

**From:** Priya Venkataraman, Director of Quality Assurance
**To:** Celeste Marchetti
**Date:** July 22, 2025
**Re:** Post-cure lots still failing

Lots shipped by Greystone on July 8 and July 14, 2025 continue to delaminate: 18% of sampled pouches failed seal integrity testing. Greystone's 30-day cure period expired on July 3, 2025. Our costs of rework, product write-offs and customer credits from the defective Greystone lots now total $286,900.

---

### Item 6 — Talbot termination letter, August 15, 2025

**From:** Celeste Marchetti, Chief Operating Officer
**To:** Harold Imbriano, President, Greystone Packaging Co.
**Date:** August 15, 2025

Greystone has failed to cure the material breach described in our June 3 notice within thirty days. Talbot hereby terminates the Packaging Supply Agreement under Section 9.2, effective immediately. Under Section 9.4, Talbot has no further minimum purchase obligations for Contract Year 3 or thereafter. Talbot reserves all rights, including to recover its damages from the nonconforming lots.

---

### Item 7 — Greystone Notice of Dispute, September 25, 2026

**From:** Bernard T. Lisowski, Lisowski Varga LLP, counsel for Greystone
**To:** General Counsel, Talbot Fresh Foods, Inc.
**Date:** September 25, 2026

This is Greystone's Notice of Dispute under Section 14.1 of the Packaging Supply Agreement concerning Talbot's failure to pay the Contract Year 2 and Contract Year 3 shortfall amounts and its wrongful termination. Greystone requests a meeting of senior executives.

---

### Item 8 — Greystone counsel letter, October 12, 2026

**From:** Bernard T. Lisowski, Lisowski Varga LLP
**To:** General Counsel, Talbot Fresh Foods, Inc.
**Date:** October 12, 2026

Enclosed please find a copy of the Complaint filed October 9, 2026, together with a Notice of a Lawsuit and Request to Waive Service of a Summons under Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(d) and two copies of the waiver form.

**File note (Talbot Legal, October 26, 2026):** Talbot did not sign or return the Rule 4(d) waiver. Greystone then served the summons and complaint on Talbot's registered agent (see docket).

## Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (summary)

- **Answer.** A defendant must serve an answer within 21 days after being served with the summons and complaint; or, if it has timely waived service under Rule 4(d), within 60 days after the request for a waiver was sent (Rule 12(a)(1)(A)).
- **Computing periods stated in days (Rule 6(a)(1)).** Exclude the day of the event that triggers the period; count every day, including intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays; include the last day of the period, but if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the period continues to run until the end of the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.
- **"Next day" (Rule 6(a)(5)).** The "next day" is determined by continuing to count forward when the period is measured after an event and backward when measured before an event.
- **Legal holidays (Rule 6(a)(6))** include, among others, Veterans Day and Thanksgiving Day.
- **Disclosure statement (Rule 7.1).** A nongovernmental corporate party must file a disclosure statement with its first appearance, pleading, petition, motion, response or other request addressed to the court.

# PROJECT LANTERN — TRANSACTION SUMMARY FOR MERGER-CONTROL COUNSEL

**Prepared by:** Altamira Health Technologies, Inc. — Corporate Development
**Date:** September 15, 2025
**Status:** Board approval obtained September 11, 2025; signing targeted for October 1, 2025

## 1. Parties

**Acquirer.** Altamira Health Technologies, Inc. ("Altamira"), a Delaware corporation headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Altamira is the ultimate parent entity of the Altamira group; no natural person or entity controls it. Altamira designs and manufactures in-vitro diagnostic instruments and consumables.

**Target.** Sorell Diagnostics B.V. ("Sorell"), a private limited company organized under the laws of the Netherlands with its registered office in Eindhoven. Sorell is the ultimate parent of its group, which includes Sorell Diagnostics USA, Inc. (a wholly owned distribution subsidiary in Raleigh, North Carolina). Sorell manufactures point-of-care coagulation analyzers and test cartridges at its Eindhoven plant.

## 2. Structure

2.1 Altamira will acquire 92% of the issued voting shares of Sorell from the Van Duren family holding company and Sorell's management shareholders, for a cash purchase price of $212,500,000 (the "Purchase Price").

2.2 Altamira already holds 8% of Sorell's voting shares, acquired in a 2022 minority investment. Corporate Development values that existing 8% stake at $16,000,000 as of today. Following closing Altamira will hold 100% of Sorell.

2.3 There is no earn-out or deferred consideration. Sorell's net debt at closing is expected to be approximately $18,000,000 and will be repaid by Sorell from cash on hand at closing; it does not form part of the Purchase Price.

## 3. Rationale and overlap

3.1 Both parties sell point-of-care coagulation analyzers to hospitals and anticoagulation clinics. Altamira's analyzer is sold mainly in the United States and Germany; Sorell's is sold mainly in the Netherlands, Germany and France. The deal team expects the combined business to be the leading supplier of point-of-care coagulation analyzers in the EEA.

3.2 Sorell's cartridge line has no overlap with Altamira's products.

## 4. Timetable

4.1 Signing: October 1, 2025. Altamira intends to submit any required United States premerger notification on October 6, 2025.

4.2 Closing is targeted for the earliest date permitted after all mandatory merger-control clearances are obtained.

## 5. Integration planning (from the Corporate Development integration workstream)

5.1 Integration planning will be conducted through a clean team for competitively sensitive information.

5.2 To capture revenue synergies quickly, Altamira's commercial team will assume responsibility for Sorell's US pricing decisions from signing, and Sorell's US sales representatives will begin reporting to Altamira's Vice President of Sales on October 1, 2025.

## 6. Questions for counsel

(a) Is a filing required under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act? If so, what is the filing fee and when would the initial waiting period expire?

(b) Does the transaction have an EU dimension under the EU Merger Regulation, and if so what are the consequences for timing?

(c) Any substantive or process concerns we should address before signing?

# MERGER-CONTROL THRESHOLD REFERENCE SHEET (INTERNAL)

**Antitrust practice group — reference figures for transactions closing in 2025.** Figures are reproduced for convenience; always confirm against the current Federal Register notice and the text of the EU Merger Regulation before advising.

## A. United States — Hart-Scott-Rodino Act (thresholds effective February 21, 2025)

A.1 **Size-of-transaction.** A transaction is potentially reportable if, as a result, the acquiring person would hold voting securities and/or assets of the acquired person valued in excess of $126.4 million. Voting securities of the same issuer already held by the acquiring person are aggregated with those being acquired (16 C.F.R. 801.13).

A.2 **Size-of-person.** For transactions valued above $126.4 million but not more than $505.8 million, the size-of-person test must also be met: generally, one person must have annual net sales or total assets of $252.9 million or more and the other person must have annual net sales or total assets of $25.3 million or more. Transactions valued above $505.8 million are reportable regardless of the size of the parties.

A.3 **Foreign issuer exemption (16 C.F.R. 802.51).** An acquisition by a U.S. person of voting securities of a foreign issuer is exempt unless the issuer (including all entities it controls) holds assets located in the United States having an aggregate total value of over $126.4 million, or made aggregate sales in or into the United States of over $126.4 million in its most recent fiscal year.

A.4 **Filing fees (2025).**

| Value of transaction | Fee |
|---|---|
| Less than $179.4 million | $30,000 |
| $179.4 million or more but less than $555.5 million | $105,000 |
| $555.5 million or more but less than $1.111 billion | $265,000 |
| $1.111 billion or more but less than $2.222 billion | $425,000 |
| $2.222 billion or more but less than $5.555 billion | $850,000 |
| $5.555 billion or more | $2,390,000 |

A.5 **Waiting period.** The initial waiting period is 30 days from filing (15 days for cash tender offers and bankruptcy sales). If the period would end on a weekend or federal holiday, it ends on the next business day. Parties may not close, and the acquirer may not obtain beneficial ownership or operational control of the target, before the waiting period expires or is terminated ("gun-jumping"; civil penalties accrue per day of violation).

## B. European Union — Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 (EUMR)

B.1 **Article 1(2).** A concentration has an EU dimension where (a) the combined aggregate worldwide turnover of all the undertakings concerned is more than EUR 5,000 million; and (b) the aggregate EU-wide turnover of each of at least two of the undertakings concerned is more than EUR 250 million; unless each of the undertakings concerned achieves more than two-thirds of its aggregate EU-wide turnover within one and the same Member State.
